newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rise but major investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rise but major investors sidelined.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange rose for a fourth consecutive day on Wednesday but brokers said most investors remained sidelined by political jitters over the Israeli-Palestinian security talks.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.29 percent to end the trading week at 148.66 points, up 1.3 percent from last Wednesday, in moderate turnover worth 673,000 dinars ($950,000).
For the second day running Arab Bank Group shares helped nudge the index upwards, accounting for over a third of Wednesday's business before closing up one dinar at 249 dinars.

Brokers said the bank, Jordan's biggest, was less vulnerable to waves of uncertainty over Middle East peace talks which have hit other shares on the market. Palestinian and Israeli negotiators are wrangling over a seven-month delay to planned Israeli troop redeployments in the West Bank town of Hebron.

"Arab Bank's probably the only multi-national stock on the exchange," said broker Nasser al-Amad. "It's a global bank with branches all over the world. If it's affected in Palestinian territories and Jordan the other branches will still perform."
The bank is also expected to benefit from proposals to drop a 15 percent tax on bonus share issues. "For those with no confidence, it's a good hedge," said Amad.
Livestock and Poultry, which brokers say has been taken over by a single investor in recent weeks, fell another 0.02 dinars to 0.66 dinars on a 107,000 dinar turnover.
Overall 14 stocks rose on Wednesday, 11 fell and 19 traded and closed unchanged.
Wednesday's volume of 673,000 dinars was the highest of the week but Amad said big investors were still steering clear.
"The volume reflects just a few people selling for cash needs and some small investors trading," he said.

The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.06 percent to 80.81 points from 80.76 points on Monday, still 15.39 percent down from the same time last year.
